notes.Project:
HandOff247 reads a project folder and writes a handoff pack for the next person: diagrams, structure, extracted comments and a map of how the tools connect. It is static analysis only (it never imports or runs the target's code) and it is standard-library Python, so `python -m handoff247` works on any machine with Python 3.10+.
Status: v0.2.0. The first real target was PlayBookOS (see examples/playbookos). C#, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, PowerShell, shell and batch have analyzers; other languages are inventoried but not parsed. Output is English; a project's own comments and headings in another language get English versions from the notes file's `## Translations` table.
notes.Topic: Successor checklist:
1. Run the tests: `python -m unittest discover -s tests`.
2. Regenerate the examples after any analyzer change: `python -m handoff247 build <PlayBookOS checkout> --name PlayBookOS -o examples/playbookos --notes examples/playbookos.notes.md --date <date>`. If an analyzer change surfaces new Korean comments or headings, `check --notes examples/playbookos.notes.md` reports them; add their rows to the Translations table there. Read the diff of the generated pages: a change there is a change in what successors will be told.
3. Regenerate this pack: `python -m handoff247 build . -o docs/handoff --date <date>`.
4. Open `index.html` of a pack in a browser and check that every diagram renders (Mermaid errors show as red text in the page).
notes.Topic: Known issues and risks:
- The rule that matters most: a wrong statement is worse than a missing one. When a pattern is ambiguous the analyzers leave it out; inferences (for example a wrapper passed in as a parameter) are labelled and drawn dashed. Keep it that way.
- Analysis is regex/lexer based for everything except Python (which uses `ast`). Code built from runtime strings, reflection or dependency-injection containers is not followed.
- MCP tool names from the C# SDK are derived from method names (snake_case, `Async` removed) and marked with * in the pack.
- Mermaid labels must go through `mermaid.esc`; `*`, `_` and backticks are escaped because Mermaid otherwise formats them as Markdown.
notes.Topic: Credentials and accounts: None. The tool needs no keys. The GitHub Action only uses the workflow's own checkout.
notes.Area: .github: CI: unit tests on Linux and Windows (Python 3.10 and 3.12), a self-documentation run, and a run of the composite action against the test fixture.
notes.Area: handoff247: The package. Data flows inventory → analyzers → connect → (mermaid, render_md, render_html) → build. pipeline.py wires the first three; cli.py and build.py the rest.
notes.Area: tests: `test_handoff.py` plus `fixtures/mini`, a small fake app (C# + JS + Python + PowerShell + batch) wired the same way as PlayBookOS: three modes, one dispatch switch, HTTP route, MCP tools, launch scripts. Every connection type the tool claims to detect has an assertion here.
notes.File: handoff247/__init__.py: Holds `__version__`; the version is printed in every generated page.
notes.File: handoff247/analyzers/__init__.py: Maps a file's language to its analyzer. An exception inside one analyzer marks only that file as "not parsed"; it never stops the run.
notes.File: handoff247/analyzers/csharp.py: The richest analyzer: types and primary-constructor dependencies, entry modes (`if (mode == "x")` in the entry file), `switch` dispatch tables with handler resolution, minimal-API routes, `[McpServerTool]` methods, environment variables and `Path.Combine` literals.
notes.File: handoff247/analyzers/docs.py: Markdown (summary, headings, relative links, code blocks for `<mode> <op>` usage), plus config formats: .csproj, package.json, pyproject, requirements, MCP client configs (`mcpServers` / `[mcp_servers]`), Dockerfile, GitHub workflows.
notes.File: handoff247/analyzers/python.py: Uses `ast`, never imports the file. Finds argparse sub-commands, subprocess launches (rendered with `{variable}` placeholders), env reads/writes, dict/if-chain/match dispatch tables, Flask/FastAPI routes and MCP tool decorators.
notes.File: handoff247/analyzers/shell.py: PowerShell, POSIX shell and batch: leading comment / .SYNOPSIS as summary, `$env:` / `export` / `set` variables, and command lines that launch something (dotnet, python, powershell -File, `&` call operator, start URL).
notes.File: handoff247/analyzers/web.py: JavaScript/TypeScript (imports, exported functions with spans, `fetch` calls, Express routes, MCP registrations, `case` tables), HTML (`<script src>`, `<link>`, inline scripts) and CSS imports.
notes.File: handoff247/build.py: Writes the pack: five Markdown pages, `diagrams/*.mmd`, `handoff.json` (its first key `"generator": "HandOff247"` is how later runs recognise and skip an old pack) and `index.html`.
notes.File: handoff247/cli.py: Three commands: `build`, `notes`, `check`. `check --min N` exits 1 when fewer than N% of files have notes, which is how CI can enforce documentation.
notes.File: handoff247/connect.py: Turns per-file facts into edges and connection maps. The key idea: string keys of a dispatch table (`"list"`, `"ontology.search"`) are followed to every caller (`api('list')`, `cli('list')`, `Call("list")`, `cli list` in docs), and each caller's wrapper function is inspected to tell HTTP, CLI process or in-process apart. A caller group only counts when it uses two or more keys or a dotted key, so ordinary strings like "git" are not mistaken for operations.
notes.File: handoff247/labels.py: Every generated heading and label, in one table, so pages and diagrams use the same words. Extracted comments and notes never pass through it.
notes.File: handoff247/inventory.py: Lists files with `git ls-files` (so .gitignore applies), falls back to a directory walk, applies `.handoffignore` and skips folders that contain an earlier pack.
notes.File: handoff247/lexer.py: Produces two views of C-like source with identical offsets: strings+comments blanked (for identifiers) and comments blanked (for literal patterns). Handles C# verbatim, interpolated and raw strings and JS template and regex literals. If a regex in an analyzer misbehaves, check the lexer view first.
notes.File: handoff247/mermaid.py: Builds the five diagrams. `system` collapses launch scripts into one node when there are more than three; `code` hides incoming arrows of shared foundations (hubs) so the rest stays readable.
notes.File: handoff247/model.py: Dataclasses: FileInfo, Symbol, Fact, Edge, Project. A Fact is one observation with a file and line; everything in the pack traces back to one.
notes.File: handoff247/notes.py: Parses and extends the notes file. `update` only appends missing headings and missing Translations rows; it never rewrites existing text. Stale headings (for deleted files) are reported, not removed.
notes.File: handoff247/render_html.py: The single-file viewer. It embeds the Markdown pages and loads marked, DOMPurify and Mermaid from jsDelivr at pinned versions. Diagram nodes are matched back to files through the `flowchart-nN-` element ids, so clicking a node opens that file's card.
notes.File: handoff247/render_md.py: The five Markdown pages. `Linker` decides how file:line references are linked: relative when the pack is inside the project, GitHub blob URLs at the exact commit when it is outside, plain text otherwise.
notes.File: handoff247/translate.py: Finds extracted prose with letters outside the Latin script (summaries, doc comments, Markdown headings, MCP tool descriptions, sub-command help, commit subjects) and swaps in the English from the notes' Translations table. Matching is exact apart from spacing, so a comment that changed later shows its original again instead of a stale translation. Identifiers such as file names are never touched.
notes.File: tests/test_handoff.py: Runs the full pipeline on a copy of the fixture outside Git, so both file-listing paths are covered.
